question: The fifth meeting of the European Political Community (EPC) and a subsequent informal European Council meeting took place on 7 and 8 November 2024 in Budapest, Hungary. According to media reports, the Dorothea Hotel, owned by Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán’s son-in-law, was explicitly recommended to participants by the Hungarian presidency of the Council of the EU. 1.
Did the Commission President and the rest of the Commission delegation stay in the recommended Dorothea Hotel while attending the EPC and European Council meetings in Budapest that week?

Were the Commission President and the services responsible for booking the accommodation aware that the recommended accommodation, the Dorothea Hotel, was owned by the Hungarian Prime Minister’s son-in-law?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.3.2025) The Commission President and the rest of the Commission delegation did not stay at the Dorothea Hotel while attending the European Political Community and European Council meetings in Budapest on 7 and 8 November 2024. There was no recommended accommodation relayed to the Commission delegation for these meetings.
